extracted.intended_audience: chemists and laboratory technicians performing quantitative experimental chemistry
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidelines for measuring masses, specific gravities, and gas volumes: selection, construction, calibration, and operation of balances, hydrostatic instruments, pèse-liqueurs, pneumatic troughs and a gasometer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh by equilibrium with standard weights (peser)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine quantities of matter by placing them in equilibrium with known comparative weights using a balance (fléau, two pans, and an indicator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspend the beam at its midpoint so the two arms are equal; add standard weights until the lever is horizontal. This basic procedure is the foundation of quantitative chemical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt decimal fractions of the pound for laboratory work
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of traditional arbitrary subdivisions (onces, gros, grains), divide the pound into tenths, hundredths, thousandths, etc., i.e., decimal fractions of the pound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using decimal divisions makes inter‑laboratory comparisons and arithmetic far simpler; the author provides a conversion table and examples converting vulgar fractions into decimals for summation and reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple balances of graded precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Have three excellent balances reserved for research plus less-precise balances for routine lab use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended: a heavy research balance (weigh to 15–20 lb without flexing), a medium research balance (18–20 ounces with 0.1 grain precision), and a very sensitive small balance (detects 1/512 grain). Additionally keep a large iron-beam balance for heavy liquid vessels (~40–50 lb to 0.5 gros), a medium balance to 8–10 lb (~12–15 grains), and a hand balance ~1 lb to grain precision for daily use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect precision balances from corrosive laboratory conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use the most accurate balances inside the laboratory where they will be exposed to acids or rust; store them in a separate cabinet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep research balances in a separate cabinet where no acids enter. Sensitive instruments must be preserved from moisture and corrosives to maintain accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify and calibrate weights frequently
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly check the standard weights used for weighing, since those supplied by commercial makers may have been adjusted against less sensitive balances and become inaccurate when tested with more perfect balances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test supplier weights on your most sensitive balances and recalibrate as needed to avoid systematic error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat weighings and cross-check with decimal and vulgar fractions
rubrics_metrics.description: To reduce weighing errors, repeat measurements and perform them using both traditional fractional units and decimal fractions of the pound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeating weighings in two representations provides a valuable cross-check and reduces arithmetic and transcription mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hydrostatic method for specific gravity (pesanteur spécifique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine specific gravity by weighing a solid in air and then when submerged in the fluid: the loss of weight equals the weight of displaced water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspend the specimen on a fine metallic filament, weigh in air and then fully submerged. Use the weight loss to compute specific gravity relative to water; useful for solids (alloys, metallic glasses) and especially for fluids to assess purity and concentration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pèse-liqueur (buoyancy cylinder) for sensitive liquid-density measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a hollow, weighted cylinder (pèse-liqueur) that nearly floats in distilled water to detect slight differences in liquid density by the additional small load required to bring it to a mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct of copper or silver, bottom-weighted with tin; must displace at least four pounds of water. Mark a reference point on its suspension rod; determine precisely the load needed at a fixed temperature in distilled water, then repeat in other fluids and compute differences per unit volume (or as decimal fractions). This method reveals small density differences missed by chemical analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use glass pèse-liqueurs for acidic liquids; metal ones only for neutral/alkaline
rubrics_metrics.description: For acids, metal pèse-liqueurs are unsuitable; glass hollow cylinders, hermetically sealed and weighted with mercury, must be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Glass cylinders are closed and provided with a capillary tube and small weighing basin; they are filled/lested with mercury and can carry a paper scale in the neck for convenient readings. Metal pèse-liqueurs only for waters with neutral or alkaline dissolved substances or specially weighted for spirits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pneumatic trough (cuve) construction and sizing
rubrics_metrics.description: A pneumatic trough (wood box lined with lead or tinned copper) must have the tabletop always covered by 1–1.5 inches of water and the reservoir (fosse) at least one foot deep in every direction for ordinary experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build the trough as large as the laboratory permits (author's main trough holds 4 cubic feet and 14 square feet of tablet). Have several troughs of different sizes and portable ones near furnaces so multiple experiments can run concurrently. Wooden troughs are economical but subject to leakage due to swelling/drying; marble troughs are recommended for mercury work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate vessels for receiving gases (glass bells and trays)
rubrics_metrics.description: Receive and transport gases in glass bells (cloches); use transport trays with rims and handles for moving them between troughs or storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For mercury-trough work, use small-diameter strong bells or eudiometers (tubes with thick bases). Provide plateaux with a rim and two handles for safe transport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer marble basins for mercury gasometry
rubrics_metrics.description: For gasometry with mercury, build the trough/basin from marble because marble is impermeable to mercury and resists cracking or joint separation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marble blocks should be hollowed to form the reservoir and a rigole; provide means to close the rigole. Maintain one marble trough as a reservoir for storing mercury—most secure against accidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-friction suspension for gasometer beam (tourillon on rollers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace the knife-edge support of a beam by a cylindrical steel pivot borne on movable rollers to convert high resistance sliding friction into low rolling friction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use large-diameter brass rollers and support points lined with rock crystal to reduce friction and allow free motion of the beam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use non-elongating flat chains or interlocked-plate chains for suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use chains that appreciably lengthen under load (e.g., some Vaucanson chains); instead use chains formed of interlocked iron plates with pins so they do not appreciably elongate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A chain that does not change length under different loads prevents measurement error in the suspended cloche.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide adjustable internal masses to vary cloche pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: In the cloche (air reservoir) provide a peripheral compartment with removable lead weights to increase the effective weight of the cloche when high pressure is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These weights allow increasing cloche pressure for special operations; such cases are rare but necessary to have the capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide gas routing tubes for filling, sampling under small bells, and delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Equip the gasometer vessel with at least three external tubes: one to introduce gas into the machine, one to pass gas under testing bells, and a third to conduct gas to distant points for combustion or other operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange the tubes so that connectors and stopcocks allow controlled introduction and removal of gases and flexible experimental setups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure internal cloche pressure by difference of water columns (Meusnier siphon)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a two‑branched siphon whose one end communicates with the external trough water and the other with the cloche interior; compare the height difference between this branch and an open reference tube to obtain the pressure difference in inches/lines of water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place a graduated copper rule between the tubes to read the difference. The arrangement measures compression (pressure) which is needed to convert gas volumes to weights because gas density depends on pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure gas temperature inside the cloche
rubrics_metrics.description: Fit a small thermometer with its bulb immersed inside the cloche and the graduation visible outside to record the temperature of the trapped gas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temperature, together with pressure, is necessary to compute gas specific gravity and convert volumes to weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensate for changing buoyancy of cloche via a sliding corrective weight (lentille)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mount a sliding weighted collar ('lentille') on a vertical rod at the beam center; by moving it up or down (via rack-and-pinion) the effective torque changes to compensate for the cloche's varying buoyancy as it sinks or rises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust the lentille position (by trial) for each desired degree of pressure so the pressure is effectively equalized across the cloche travel. Record the correction height for each pressure in a register; the correction need only be approximate within a quarter to a half line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure gas quantity by beam angular deflection using a graduated arc and nonius
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix a graduated copper arc (limbe) on the beam and measure its angular descent with a fixed index equipped with a nonius giving hundredths of a degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibrate volumes by filling a bottle of known capacity (weigh water to determine its capacity), set machine to zero pressure, then pass gas to fill the bottle while reading the limbe to determine the gas volume supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational protocol: fix water level and calibrate prior to use
rubrics_metrics.description: Always fill the external vase to a predetermined level with the beam horizontal; determine lentille positions for constant pressure by trial; record all calibration settings in a register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and keep the same water level for all experiments; trial adjustments of the lentille and registration of settings are required for reproducible gasometry at different pressures.
